lessons.title: Slope measures change
lessons.reading: Slope is change in y divided by change in x. Use the same point order in both subtractions.
lessons.easyReading: Slope is change in y divided by change in x. Use the same point order in both subtractions.
lessons.expertReading: Slope is change in y divided by change in x. Use the same point order in both subtractions. A vertical line has undefined slope because its horizontal change is zero.

application.explanation: 2. Slope is change in y divided by change in x. Use the same point order in both subtractions.

vocab.definition: The rate of vertical change per unit horizontal change.

lessons.practice: Explain how slope helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 2. Slope is change in y divided by change in x. Use the same point order in both subtractions.

lessons.title: Read a linear rule
lessons.reading: In y = mx + b, m is slope and b is the output at x = 0. A starting value and a rate play different roles.
lessons.easyReading: In y = mx + b, m is slope and b is the output at x = 0. A starting value and a rate play different roles.
lessons.expertReading: In y = mx + b, m is slope and b is the output at x = 0. A starting value and a rate play different roles. A linear rule is proportional precisely when its intercept is zero.
lessons.worked: In y = 3x + 4, the line starts at y = 4 and rises three per unit of x.
steps: In y = 3x + 4, the line starts at y = 4 and rises three per unit of x.

application.prompt: What is the y-intercept of y = 2x − 5?
application.explanation: −5. In y = mx + b, m is slope and b is the output at x = 0. A starting value and a rate play different roles.

lessons.title: Solve both sides
lessons.reading: Collect variable terms on one side and constants on the other using equal operations. Then isolate the variable.
lessons.easyReading: Collect variable terms on one side and constants on the other using equal operations. Then isolate the variable.
lessons.expertReading: Collect variable terms on one side and constants on the other using equal operations. Then isolate the variable. An identity is true for every permitted input, while a contradiction has no solution.
lessons.worked: For 3x + 2 = x + 10, subtract x and two: 2x = 8, so x = 4.
steps: For 3x + 2 = x + 10, subtract x and two: 2x = 8, so x = 4.

application.explanation: x = 5. Collect variable terms on one side and constants on the other using equal operations. Then isolate the variable.

vocab.definition: Equations with the same solution set.

lessons.practice: Explain how equivalent equations helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.

lessons.title: Right-triangle lengths
lessons.reading: For a right triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse opposite the right angle. Check which side is unknown.
lessons.easyReading: For a right triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse opposite the right angle. Check which side is unknown.
lessons.expertReading: For a right triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse opposite the right angle. Check which side is unknown. The converse theorem tests whether given lengths form a right triangle.
lessons.worked: Legs of 3 and 4 give c² = 9 + 16 = 25, so c = 5.
steps: Legs of 3 and 4 give c² = 9 + 16 = 25, so c = 5.

lessons.title: Exponent patterns
lessons.reading: Multiplying powers with the same base adds exponents because it combines repeated factors. This rule does not apply to adding powers.
lessons.easyReading: Multiplying powers with the same base adds exponents because it combines repeated factors. This rule does not apply to adding powers.
lessons.expertReading: Multiplying powers with the same base adds exponents because it combines repeated factors. This rule does not apply to adding powers. The quotient rule subtracts exponents for a nonzero base.
lessons.worked: 2³ × 2² = 2⁵ because there are five factors of two.
steps: 2³ × 2² = 2⁵ because there are five factors of two.

application.explanation: x⁷. Multiplying powers with the same base adds exponents because it combines repeated factors. This rule does not apply to adding powers.

vocab.definition: A number indicating how many repeated factors of a base are used for a positive integer power.

lessons.practice: Explain how exponent helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: x⁷. Multiplying powers with the same base adds exponents because it combines repeated factors. This rule does not apply to adding powers.
